# I2
Verdict: reject
CRITICAL: 0
MAJOR: 2
Headline: The supplied record leaves the robot-specific experiment uncovered, but supports neither an independently valuable adaptation nor adequate comparative validation (candidate.json; prior_work.md).
Occupation: prior_work.md identifies DTR §2 as covering cost-dependent retention and protection of unrecoverable information, GreedyDual as covering retrieval-cost allocation, and the human-memory studies as covering access-dependent encoding. Its robot essay also discusses reachability, retrieval cost and active re-observation. These sources do not establish the particular learned robot writer and reversible/one-way delivery interaction proposed in candidate.json; coverage is therefore not-covered within the supplied record.
Experiment: candidate.json specifies 2,000 simulated training episodes, one A100-day, 200 paired test episodes per route condition, matched histories/backbone/eight slots/action budget, route-cost shuffling, and explicit interaction and overall-gain kill conditions. This is a concrete bounded falsification plan. Its predicted ten-point gain is not an observation, and the stated thresholds are decision rules rather than evidence of likely success.
Estimand: MAJOR 2 concerns comparative validity: candidate.json compares only validation-best surprise, recency and uniform writing. prior_work.md supplies a directly relevant learned writing comparator, MemER, and a simple substantive alternative, retrieval-cost allocation from GreedyDual. Faithful task adaptations are needed to establish an attributable improvement over existing approaches. The route interaction and shuffled-cost control can test conditional usefulness of the cost signal, but cannot establish superiority to those omitted alternatives; a public ranking for this new protocol is unnecessary (review_contract.md).
Payoff: MAJOR 1 concerns independent contribution value: candidate.json proposes allocating writes using predicted revisit cost and testing recoverability as the governing variable, but specifies no setting-forced allocation mechanism beyond that transfer. prior_work.md already supports the governing principle through DTR, access-cost experiments and the robot design essay. Physical cost prediction and the delivery interaction remain distinct, but the packet supplies no concrete adaptation or argument explaining a new capability or knowledge payoff beyond applying that principle. This is insufficient support for either positive standard; it is not contrary evidence that the proposed writer would work, and the absence of completed experiments is not itself the defect.
Feasibility: The simulation scale and one-A100-day budget in candidate.json provide a reasonable bounded first-paper experiment; neither supplied research artifact establishes an execution dependency that makes this budget impossible. No CRITICAL resource or execution failure is supported.
History: unavailable; no verified history_summary.json was supplied.
Assessment: {"coverage":"not-covered","coverage_evidence":[{"source":"candidate","quote":"Test 200 paired episodes each with reversible and one-way routes."},{"source":"prior-work","quote":"none of the works read establishes the particular learned robot writer and route-interaction result."}],"causes":[{"code":"value-insufficient","evidence":[{"source":"candidate","quote":"Summary: Allocate writes using predicted revisit cost."},{"source":"candidate","quote":"Why It May Be Novel: Test recoverability as the variable governing memory allocation."},{"source":"prior-work","quote":"Both cost-dependent retention and preservation of unrecoverable information are explicit mechanisms."},{"source":"prior-work","quote":"§6 proposes choosing economically among preservation, compression, attenuation, and active re-observation. §5 includes topological reachability and retrieval cost among memory-selection considerations."}]},{"code":"design-invalid","evidence":[{"source":"candidate","quote":"Compare revisit-cost writing with validation-best surprise, recency and uniform writing."},{"source":"prior-work","quote":"This is a directly relevant learned writing baseline for retaining object-location observations and reducing repeated bin searches."},{"source":"prior-work","quote":"GreedyDual assigns cached items a retrieval-cost value, evicts the lowest-value item, and ages the remaining values; GreedyDual-Size incorporates item size through cost/size."}]}]}
Reason: Reject because the residual transfer lacks an independently supported technical or knowledge contribution (MAJOR 1), while the planned comparison omits capable learned and cost-aware alternatives (MAJOR 2); adding those comparators would repair validation but would not alone establish the retained research value required for accept-w-rev (candidate.json; prior_work.md; review_contract.md).
